trials.notes: Used WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment(), walked tokens structurally, tracked heading depth, accumulated only #text tokens with get_modifiable_text(), and handled virtual/implied closers. All called API methods are present in the rendered docs and execution recorded no _doing_it_wrong notices.

Correctly chose the HTML Processor and used documented token/depth/text APIs. Minor adherence issues: it initialized heading text by calling get_modifiable_text() on an ordinary heading opener, despite the docs saying ordinary container text lives in #text child tokens, and it used a lexicographic H1..H6 string range instead of an exact tag-name set. That passed the frozen tests but would misclassify tags such as H10.

Correctly chose the HTML Processor, used only documented methods, collected only #text token text, and relied on documented virtual closing tokens for malformed/implied heading closes. Slightly less explicit than the depth-boundary recipe because it flushes only on closer tags, but that is still supported by the next_token() contract.

failure_analysis: All three trials passed all 7 frozen cases, with no _doing_it_wrong records. The docs worked well for this task: the processor-choice guidance explicitly says to use WP_HTML_Processor for collecting element text, walking subtrees, and handling implied/missing closing tags; create_fragment() explains BODY fragments; next_token() documents that it visits text and virtual closers; get_current_depth() explains the >= subtree boundary; and get_modifiable_text() states that #text values are already decoded. Near-misses were in trial-2: it appeared to think an ordinary heading opener might carry text, and it matched H1-H6 with lexical string comparisons rather than exact names. Those did not affect the hidden cases, but they point to places where the API docs could be harder to misuse.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs say element names are uppercase dynamic names, but do not warn that callers matching a finite element family should not use lexicographic string ranges. Trial-2 used 'H1' <= name <= 'H6', which also accepts H10.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short note or example showing exact set membership for finite tag groups, e.g. compare against an array/set of allowed uppercase names rather than string ordering.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs contain the correct rule, but a candidate still called get_modifiable_text() on an ordinary container opener as if it might contain descendant text.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Move a concrete contrast into the method docblock summary: ordinary element openers such as DIV/P/SPAN return an empty string; their descendant text is read from #text tokens, while TITLE/TEXTAREA/SCRIPT/STYLE are the special opener-carried cases.

doc_gaps.problem: The rendered docs explain both closer-driven flushing and depth-boundary loops, but the relationship between the two patterns is spread across examples.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a compact 'subtree extraction checklist' near next_token(): record opener depth, collect only selected token types, exit on depth below opener depth or flush on the matching/virtual closer, then decide whether paused_at_incomplete_token()/get_last_error() matters for the caller.
